blocks.text: Acreage and rural land in Fort Langley
What trades is individual fee-simple parcels — village lots in the core and acreage-edge lots outside it — read parcel by parcel for ALR status, flood, and well/septic servicing.

items.t: Acreage lots sit on the village edges, mainly south and east toward the Salmon River valley; farm land on the village edges is in the ALR in places — confirm a parcel on the ALC maps before valuing any farm, coach-house or subdivision angle.

Village fee-simple lots (the default form around the acreage edges): The established village stock is freehold houses on fee-simple lots under the Fort Langley Community Plan and Zoning Bylaw No. 2500; downtown-core lots also sit inside the Heritage Conservation Area. Village residential zoning includes R-1E, named for the village in a Township public-hearing document.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect acreage buyers in Fort Langley

items.t: BC Assessment farm class: Gross annual value of at least $2,500 (farm area 0.8–4 ha); $2,500 plus 5% of the actual value of the area over 4 ha (>4 ha); $10,000 (<0.8 ha); application delivered to the assessor on or before October 31.

Flood diligence: Ask the Township for the parcel's flood information before purchase; the Salmon River Pump Station's flood box gates close when Fraser River levels rise, and Council has authorized detailed design and tendering for pump station upgrades. For any strata purchase, also check the Form B insurance summary for flood coverage/deductibles.

blocks.text: Good to know about Fort Langley

items.t: Heritage approval can outrank zoning on a core lot: Price core land on the heritage path, not just the zone.

The Salmon River Pump Station provides the community's protection — including, per the Township, mitigation of flooding of Fort Langley's agricultural lands during freshet — its gates close as Fraser levels rise, and upgrades are in detailed design/tendering. An acreage's protection story is municipal infrastructure plus the parcel's own flood information, not a seller's assurance.
Poppy Secondary with no middle school shown — a buyer mapping schools for an edge parcel should run that parcel's own address rather than assume a three-tier chain.

faq.q: What kind of acreage can I actually buy in Fort Langley?
faq.a: Individual fee-simple acreage-edge parcels south and east toward the Salmon River valley — some of them ALR farm land — bought one parcel at a time. There is no acreage subdivision or acreage development product here, and no bare-land strata. Village lots (heritage-gated in the core) and Bedford Landing lots (tenure read address by address) are the other land forms.

faq.q: Is a Bedford Landing lot fee-simple or strata?
faq.a: Either exists under the same community name: row homes are recorded fee-simple (Row House (Non-Strata)); the strata buildings are separate. The civic address and title decide — never the "Bedford Landing" label.

faq.q: Can I subdivide or add units to a village or edge lot?
faq.a: The Township's SSMUH bylaw (6020, Nov 18, 2024) amended the single-family/duplex zones and has no six-unit tier; in the village the Heritage Conservation Area, Development Permit Area and Design Guidelines sit on top of it. Subdivision runs under Servicing Bylaw 5382 (2019). On ALR land, subdivision additionally needs ALC approval.

faq.q: Can I build a coach house on an edge lot?
faq.a: A coach house under Zoning Bylaw 2500 s. 102 is a fee-simple second unit on the same title — never a separate strata lot or separate sale. On ALR land, the ALC's additional-residence caps (90 m² ≤40 ha / 186 m² >40 ha) and Township bylaws both apply, and ALR residences cannot be stratified. A flagged live s. 102 conflict means: confirm the current text with the Township first.
